checks: If two coefficient vectors each sum to one and give gradient zero, their difference is a linear combination of the k−1 independent difference rows with coefficients given by its first k−1 entries. They vanish, proving uniqueness even if some of the balancing weights are zero.

At r₀ all profile differences vanish. Their derivative has rank k−1, so the C² implicit function theorem gives the local level-set manifold with exactly the displayed tangent kernel. A coordinate line in a local chart realizes every tangent velocity.

On a tie curve the derivatives of all profile compositions coincide. Averaging the first derivatives gives zero by stationarity. Averaging their second chain rules eliminates the curve acceleration, leaving the probability-weighted Hessians on the same velocity.

A negative second derivative gives strict decrease by Taylor expansion along the exact tie curve, and the assumed touching upper envelopes and persistent competing-candidate gap transfer it to the actual normalized maximum. If the tangent space is zero the sign test is vacuous. The k=1 case reduces to the ordinary stationary Hessian test.
